draft.title: Maxwell and electromagnetic waves
card: In the 1860s James Clerk Maxwell combined the laws of electricity and magnetism into one set of equations. They showed that a changing electric field produces a changing magnetic field, and the reverse.

Maxwell's equations predicted that these linked fields can travel through space together as a wave, with no medium needed. The electric and magnetic fields oscillate at right angles to each other and to the direction the wave travels.
The predicted speed depends only on two constants, the permittivity and permeability of free space: c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀). This gives about 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s, the measured speed of light.
Maxwell concluded that light is an electromagnetic wave. Heinrich Hertz later produced and detected radio waves in the laboratory, and they behaved as Maxwell predicted.
draft.remember: Changing fields sustain each other as a wave, and its predicted speed matches light.

a.q: Why did Maxwell conclude that light is an electromagnetic wave?
opts: His predicted wave speed matched the measured speed of light
Light was shown to need a medium, as sound does
Light was found to carry electric charge from the source
His equations showed that only static fields can travel
a.why: His equations gave a wave speed of about 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s from two constants, matching the measured speed of light. The medium option is wrong because these waves need no medium to travel.
a.clue: Compare the predicted speed with a measured one.

b.q: A student says that an electromagnetic wave in a vacuum is a changing electric field travelling alone, with no magnetic field. Which reply matches Maxwell's prediction?
opts: The changing electric and magnetic fields travel together
The magnetic field only appears when the wave meets matter
The magnetic field travels first, then the electric field
The student is right, as only the electric field oscillates
b.why: Maxwell showed that a changing electric field produces a changing magnetic field and the reverse, so each sustains the other as the wave travels. The wave does not need matter for the magnetic part to exist.
b.clue: Each changing field produces the other.

a.best: His predicted wave speed matched the measured speed of light

b.best: The changing electric and magnetic fields travel together
